title: Ringed geometric-point evaluation with signed tensor and coefficient models
statement:
Let $k$ be algebraically closed, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and use the small pro-etale site and geometric stalk of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk]. For a sheaf of commutative rings $B$ on this site put $R=B(s)$. The topos point associated to $\operatorname{id}_s$ has inverse image canonically identified with final-object sections, by the restriction maps $\mathcal F(U)\to\mathcal F(s)$ along pointed lifts $s\to U$. With the identity ring map to $R$, its module pullback is canonically $\Gamma_s=\Gamma(s,-)$, and its total derived pullback is the functor induced by termwise exact sections [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact].
For K-flat complexes $P,Q$ of $B$-modules with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], there is a natural chain isomorphism
$$ b_{P,Q}:\Gamma_s\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_B Q)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tot}(\Gamma_sP\otimes_R\Gamma_sQ). $$
Its inverse sends $x\otimes y$ to the section tensor of $x,y$. The image complexes are K-flat with flat terms. After localization this is precisely the canonical ringed-topos derived pullback comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], identified through exact sections, including its representative comparison maps. This identification is natural in both derived variables and independent of the K-flat models.
The unit comparison is $\Gamma_s B=R$. The maps $b$ intertwine the signed total-complex associators, both unitors and braiding: in degrees $i,j$ the braiding is $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{ij}y\otimes x$, the associator preserves the order of the three generators, and the unitors are multiplication. These are equalities of the specified chain maps and descend to their derived maps. For a morphism $B\to B'$ of commutative ring sheaves, putting $R'=B'(s)$, the square between these tensor comparisons and the canonical derived scalar comparisons commutes. On flat-term models its inverse form is the balanced rule $(x\otimes a)\otimes(y\otimes b)\mapsto(x\otimes y)\otimes ab$; the squares include identity and composed scalar maps.
For the coefficient sheaves of [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], this identifies $\Gamma_s(A_{E,n})_s=A_{E,n}$ and $\Gamma_s\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s}=\mathcal O_E$ with the specified constant-section and quotient maps. The integral assertion here concerns the ordinary ambient tensor, before completion.

proof.text: Apply [lem-fix-geometric-stalk-topos-point] to $Y=s$ and $\bar y=\operatorname{id}_s$. Its inverse image is the pointed-neighbourhood colimit of [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk]. The object $(s,\operatorname{id}_s)$ is initial in that neighbourhood category: its unique pointed arrow to $(U,u)$ is $u:s\to U$. It is therefore terminal in the opposite index. Explicitly send a representative $(U,u,z)$ to $u^*z\in\mathcal F(s)$ and send $w\in\mathcal F(s)$ to its class at $(s,\operatorname{id})$. Pointed-arrow compatibility makes the first map well-defined; the colimit relation for $u$ makes the two maps inverse. This proves the claimed natural identification, with precisely the restriction maps specified in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0991, section-points, paragraph before lemma-classical-point (Tag 0993); explicit initial-object specialization

proof.text: The same restriction formulas respect addition, multiplication and module actions, since all those operations in [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk] are computed on common representatives. Hence $p^{-1}B=R=B(s)$ with its actual ring operations. Equip this point with $p^{-1}B\to R$ equal to the identity. By the module-pullback formula in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], $p^*M=R\otimes_Rp^{-1}M\cong M(s)$ via $a\otimes x\mapsto ax$, with inverse $x\mapsto1\otimes x$. These maps are natural on module morphisms. Thus the actual module pullback is $\Gamma_s$. It is exact and its termwise functor preserves quasi-isomorphisms by [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact].

proof.text: Use [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence] for this ringed point, presenting $\mathbf{Set}$ by the one-object trivial site and $R$ as its ring sheaf. Its cochain isomorphism $c_{p;P,Q}$, through step 2, is $b_{P,Q}$. Its inverse sends $x\otimes y$ to the section tensor of $x,y$: substitute $1\otimes x$ and $1\otimes y$ in the displayed inverse formula for $c$. This holds on every bidegree summand, including arbitrary direct-sum total degrees. On a generator of bidegree $(i,j)$, the differential on either side is $dx\otimes y+(-1)^i x\otimes dy$, since the coefficient factors have degree zero. The cited lemma supplies the isomorphism and its naturality; this calculation fixes the direction and normalization of the specified chain map.

source.place: Tag 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product, displayed total-complex map; sites-modules.tex Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback

proof.text: For flat-term K-flat $P,Q$, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] says that $p^*P$ and $p^*Q$ are K-flat with flat terms. Under step 2 these are $\Gamma_sP,\Gamma_sQ$. By [lem-pur-kflat-total-tensor-model], $T=\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_BQ)$ is itself flat-term K-flat and represents the derived tensor. Apply [lem-pur-exact-pullback-signed-comparison] to the exact $p^*=\Gamma_s$ of step 2. Its isomorphism $\eta:Lp^*\cong D(\Gamma_s)$ identifies the resolving comparison on every flat-term K-flat complex with the termwise sections comparison. Its displayed representative square identifies the canonical derived tensor comparison with the localization of the specific $b_{P,Q}$ of step 3, including the representative maps for $P,Q,T$. The uniqueness and naturality in that lemma give independence of K-flat resolutions and naturality for all derived morphisms.

source.place: Tags 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat), 07A2 (lemma-tensor-product-K-flat), 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change), and 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), with the cited representative-normalized exact-functor refinement

proof.text: The unit isomorphism is the actual equality $\Gamma_sB=R$. The constraint equations of [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence] apply before localization. More explicitly, under $b^{-1}$ the associativity square sends $(x\otimes y)\otimes z$ to the section $x\otimes(y\otimes z)$ along either route. The symmetry square sends $x\otimes y$ in degrees $(i,j)$ to $(-1)^{ij}$ times the section $y\otimes x$ along either route. The two unit squares send $a\otimes x$ or $x\otimes a$ to $ax$. The coefficient-unit identification of step 2 sends $1\otimes a$ to $a$, so these are the specified unitors. These are equalities of chain maps, with the same signs on each summand, rather than just existence of compatible constraints.

source.place: Tag 07A4 total-complex construction and Tag 03EL; explicit constraint equations of the cited cochain-coherence lemma

proof.text: For $B\to B'$ use in [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence] the coefficient square $p^{-1}B\to p^{-1}B'$ over $R\to R'=B'(s)$, with both vertical ring maps the identities. The square commutes because the restriction maps of step 1 are natural also in ring sheaves. The cited $\kappa$ and tensor/scalar equation give the requested square with the canonical scalar comparisons. In its inverse form, both routes on a homogeneous generator send $(x\otimes a)\otimes(y\otimes b)$ to the section $(x\otimes y)\otimes ab$. This uses balancing over $R$ and multiplication in $R'$; the new scalars have degree zero, so there is no extra sign. For $B\to B'\to B''$, the scalar-association maps send $(x\otimes a)\otimes b$ to $x\otimes ab$; the composition equation of the same lemma applies, and the iterated tensor square sends the two coefficient factors to their product in $B''(s)$. For an identity ring map these are multiplication unitors. This verifies the identity and composed scalar squares at chain level, with no flatness assumption on the coefficient map.

source.place: Tag 07A4 and sites-modules.tex Tag 03EL; coefficient and composition equations of the cited cochain-coherence refinement

proof.text: Localize the equations in steps 5 and 6 using flat-term K-flat models. [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] identifies their localization with the derived category and its specified tensor representatives; [lem-pur-kflat-total-tensor-model] keeps every iterated tensor in the resolving class. For scalar extension, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] applied to the identity topos with coefficient map $B\to B'$ (and to $R\to R'$ on the one-object site) supplies flat-term K-flat images even when the coefficient map is not flat. Consequently these are representatives for the derived scalar comparisons, rather than a claim that scalar extension is exact. The localization universal property [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property], applied successively in each variable, preserves composition and equality of these transformations and makes them natural for localized morphisms. Step 4 pins the localized tensor comparison to the canonical one. Thus all the chain constraint and scalar equations descend to the required derived equations, independently of models.

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 06YU (definition-derived-tor), 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat), and 07A4; categories.tex Tag 04VG with the cited localization universal property

proof.text: For the coefficient datum of [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], the valuation-ring and uniformizer hypotheses are supplied by [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr]. By [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients], each $A_{E,n}$ is finite. Apply [lem-pur-proetale-finite-constant-sections] with $X=V=s$ and $A=A_{E,n}$. Since $|s|$ is a singleton, evaluation of a continuous function at its unique point identifies $(A_{E,n})_s(s)$ with $A_{E,n}$. The cited comparison sends every constant-presheaf element to its constant function, so the inverse is exactly the constant-section map. For a coefficient homomorphism $A_{E,m}\to A_{E,n}$, naturality of sheafification sends the constant section $a$ to the constant section of its image. These elements exhaust the sections, so the induced section map is precisely the quotient homomorphism.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.12, discrete-space assertion; coefficient hypotheses and finite quotients from the cited arithmetic nodes

proof.text: By [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and the sectionwise limit formula of [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit], $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s}(s)=\varprojlim_n A_{E,n}$, with coordinate projections. The canonical map $\mathcal O_E\to\varprojlim_n A_{E,n}$ is an isomorphism: choose representatives $a_n\in\mathcal O_E$ for a compatible tuple. Then $a_m-a_n\in\varpi_E^n\mathcal O_E$ for $m\ge n$, hence $|a_m-a_n|_E\le|\varpi_E|_E^n\to0$. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-complete] they converge to $a\in E$. The closed balls $\mathcal O_E$ and $a_n+\varpi_E^n\mathcal O_E$ contain the appropriate tails, so $a\in\mathcal O_E$ and has the given residues. Injectivity follows from $|a|_E\le|\varpi_E|_E^n$ for all $n$. Here $0<|\varpi_E|_E<1$ follows from [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr]. The forward map is $a\mapsto(a\bmod\varpi_E^n)_n$; it is a ring homomorphism, so its inverse is also one. Together with step 8 this identifies the constant-section and every quotient map exactly. Applying steps 3--7 to this ring sheaf uses its ordinary ambient tensor, as asserted.
